members.name: SetEnergyGate
members.signature: void SetEnergyGate(float openRms, float closeRms, float holdSeconds)
members.doc:
Open-mic energy gate. Opens at openRms, closes only below closeRms
(hysteresis against a voice sitting on the threshold) and holds open for
holdSeconds after the last loud frame so word gaps do not chop.

members.name: SetInputGain
members.doc:
Linear gain applied to captured samples before the gate reads their
energy, so raising it opens the gate on a quiet microphone instead of
only making an already-transmitting voice louder.

members.name: SetProcessorSettings
members.doc:
Echo cancellation, noise suppression and automatic gain, run on every
captured frame before the gate reads it and before it is encoded — the
gate then opens on speech rather than on a fan, and nobody hears
themselves come back out of someone's speakers.

members.name: IsPlatformMuted
members.doc:
Mute and deafen mirrored from the player's platform voice client
(Discord) while voice.FollowPlatformMute is on. Kept apart from the
in-game mute so unmuting in Discord never unmutes a player who muted
here as well.

members.name: SetPeerMuted
members.doc:
Playback. Muting takes effect on what is already in flight too: the
speaker's queued packets and the samples waiting in its playback stream
are dropped, its radios close, and anything kept of its voice for
mimicry is forgotten.

members.name: SetHearingRange
members.doc: Proximity

members.name: SetProximityHysteresis
members.doc:
Fraction of MaxDistance added to the LEAVE threshold. 0.15 means a peer
enters the relay set at MaxDistance and only leaves past 1.15x it.

members.name: EvaluateAttenuation
members.doc:
Gain a listener at `distance` hears a proximity speaker at, 0..1. The
same inverse-with-rolloff curve miniaudio's default attenuation applies,
evaluated on the CPU so the relay decision and the test can agree with
what the mixer does.

members.name: IsAudibleTo
members.signature: bool IsAudibleTo(uint32_t speakerPeerId, uint32_t listenerPeerId, EVoiceTransmitChannel channel)
members.doc:
True when `listenerPeerId` is inside the speaker's hearing range,
hysteresis included. Radio always returns true. Unresolvable positions
fail OPEN — a missing pawn must not silence a player.

members.name: SetDistanceLowPass
members.doc:
Three layers, each a different cue, so a listener can tell a far voice
from a walled one: distance takes level and top end (the low-pass slides
from nearHz at MinDistance to farHz at MaxDistance, interpolated in log
frequency), occlusion takes level and top end by the wall's material,
and grain takes fidelity — past startFraction of the hearing range the
voice breaks up, reaching maxAmount at its edge. A nearHz at or above
19999 Hz with an equal farHz switches the distance low-pass off; a
maxAmount of 0 switches grain off.

members.name: SetRadioCarrierProvider
members.doc:
Radio speakers. The provider lists every carrier and where their radio
hangs; without one the only radio is the listener's own, at the listener.
Another carrier's radio is audible out to the speaker range.

members.name: EvaluateRadioAttenuation
members.doc:
Gain a listener at `distance` hears another carrier's radio at: full out
to a metre, the inverse law to the speaker range, silence past it.

members.name: SetOcclusionSmoothing
members.doc:
How fast a voice glides onto a new occlusion target, per second. Zero or
less means the shared rate from the occlusion table.

members.name: SetBytesPerSecondBudget
members.doc:
Bandwidth. A hard per-client cap in bytes/second over the outgoing voice
stream; frames over budget are DROPPED, never queued — a queued voice
frame is a stale voice frame.

Every frame handed to a speaker's playback stream, after decode and

members.name: SetPlaybackTap
members.signature: void SetPlaybackTap(const char* owner, FPlaybackTap tap)
members.doc:
Keyed taps for features that live with the scene (auto-subtitles): one
per owner, re-registering replaces, null removes. They hear what the
player hears — a muted or deafened speaker is silence here too.

members.name: SetMimicryConsent
members.doc:
Mimicry. The local player's consent to have their voice kept as short
fragments by whoever hosts the creature (voice.MimicryConsent, on by
default — the opt-out lives on the player's settings screen), stamped on
every frame this client sends. Capture is the receiving side's choice
(voice.MimicryCapture, off by default): only a host that runs a mimic
turns it on, and it keeps only consenting, unmuted talkers.

members.name: OcclusionLayerMask

The layers a voice occlusion ray may stop on — FSoundOcclusion's, so a
voice and a world sound stop on the same bodies.

types.name: FVoiceFragmentBuffer
types.doc:
FVoiceFragmentBuffer — short clips of what other players actually said, for
a creature that answers in their voices. It keeps utterances, not a stream:
a run of voiced frames becomes one fragment when the talker pauses, a run
too short to be a word is thrown away, and each player keeps only their
last few.

What it promises, because this is the one place voice is kept at all:
- memory only: nothing here writes, logs or uploads a sample;
- only from a talker whose own client stamped consent on the frame — a
frame without it drops everything held for that talker at once;
- never from a muted talker, and never while the listener is deafened
(FVoiceChatSystem gates both before a frame gets here);
- gone with the session: Shutdown, a peer leaving and a mute all forget.

types.name: FVoiceGrainFilter
types.doc:
FVoiceGrainFilter — the third layer of proximity voice, after distance and
walls: the voice breaking up as it reaches the edge of what carries. Lower
fidelity rather than lower level, so a far voice is still there but the
words smear: the sample rate is held down (sample-and-hold), the word length
is cut, and a crackle rides the voice's own envelope so silence stays silent.

Amount 0 is a bit-exact copy, so a near voice pays nothing for the layer.
Deterministic for a given seed and input: the noise is a xorshift, not the
C library's generator, so the same frames come out on every machine.

Stateful per stream, like the radio filter.

members.name: Push
members.signature: bool Push(uint16_t sequence, const int16_t* samples, uint32_t sampleCount)
members.doc:
Inserts one raw decoded frame at its sequence position. False when the
frame was refused — a duplicate, a frame older than what has already
played, or an overflow past maxFrames (the oldest is dropped to make room).

members.name: PushPacket
members.signature: bool PushPacket(uint16_t sequence, const uint8_t* payload, size_t len)
members.doc: Inserts one encoded packet, decoded later by Pop(decoder, ...).

members.name: Pop
members.doc:
Fills `out` with the next raw frame. True when a real frame was
delivered, false when the buffer concealed (hole or starvation) — `out`
is still filled in both cases, so the playback path never has to branch.

members.name: Pop
members.doc:
Decodes the next packet through `decoder`. A hole is rebuilt from the
packet after it (FEC for one frame, deep redundancy further back) when
that packet is already here, and concealed by the decoder otherwise.
True for a real or rebuilt frame, false for a concealed one.

members.name: SequenceDelta
members.signature: static int32_t SequenceDelta(uint16_t a, uint16_t b)
members.doc:
Sequence distance that treats the 16-bit counter as circular, so a
wrap does not read as a 65000-frame jump backwards.

members.name: kDefaultBitrate
members.doc:
32 kbps, not the 24 speech alone would need: deep redundancy takes its
share out of the same budget, and at 24 kbps libopus decides it cannot
afford two DRED chunks and sends none at all.

members.name: kDefaultRedundancyMs
members.doc:
Half a second of deep redundancy covers the loss bursts a relayed session
actually sees (a Wi-Fi retry storm, a route change) for a few kbps.

members.name: kMaxEncodedBytes
members.doc:
The ceiling handed to opus_encode, so a VBR peak can never write past
the reserve or overflow the wire header's 16-bit payload length. 400
bytes is Opus's own recommendation for a 20 ms mono packet.

members.name: kDtxMaxBytes
members.doc: Opus emits one or two bytes for a frame it decided not to transmit.

members.name: IsAvailable
members.doc:
False when the Opus binaries were not vendored for this platform. The
class still links; every call simply fails.

members.name: TryCreate

nullptr when Opus is unavailable or the encoder/decoder refused to come

members.name: CreateDecoder
members.doc:
A stream decoder with its own Opus state, FEC, deep redundancy and
packet-loss concealment. nullptr when Opus is unavailable.

members.name: SetBitrate
members.doc:
Target bitrate for the VBR encoder, redundancy included. It leaves the
12 KB/s per-client budget mostly unspent.

members.name: SetExpectedPacketLoss
members.doc:
What the encoder assumes about the channel. FEC only spends bits when
this is non-zero, so a session with no loss pays nothing for it.

members.name: SetRedundancyMilliseconds
members.doc:
Deep redundancy (DRED): up to this many milliseconds of past speech ride
in every packet at a low bitrate, so a burst of loss is rebuilt from the
first packet after it instead of concealed. 0 turns it off. Returns false
when the linked Opus was built without DRED.

types.name: FVoiceProcessorSettings
types.doc:
What the microphone path cleans up before a frame is encoded. Each stage can
be switched off on its own: a headset user has no echo to cancel, a studio
microphone wants no noise gate fighting it.

members.name: echoCancellation
members.doc:
Cancels the other players' voices coming back in through the microphone
from open speakers — the echo everyone else hears as themselves.

members.name: noiseSuppression
members.doc: Stationary noise (fans, hum, hiss) learned and subtracted.

members.name: autoGain
members.doc: Levels a quiet or a loud microphone toward one speaking level.

members.name: noiseSuppressDb
members.doc: How far noise is pushed down, dB below its level (negative).

members.name: autoGainTarget
members.doc: The speaking level automatic gain aims for, as a fraction of full scale.

members.name: autoGainMaxDb
members.doc: The most automatic gain will ever add, in dB.

members.name: echoTailSeconds
members.doc:
How long an echo the canceller can model — speaker-to-microphone path
plus the device buffers.

types.name: FVoiceProcessor
types.doc:
FVoiceProcessor — SpeexDSP's echo canceller and speech preprocessor around
one voice capture stream, 20 ms frame in, 20 ms frame out.

The far end the canceller subtracts is fed in by the caller, one frame per
frame of voice it played; this processor keeps a short queue of them and
takes one per captured frame, so small drift between the playback and
capture clocks is absorbed rather than warned about. With nothing played
there is nothing to cancel, and the canceller is skipped rather than run
against silence.

members.name: Configure
members.signature: bool Configure(uint32_t sampleRate, uint32_t frameSamples, const FVoiceProcessorSettings& settings)
members.doc:
Rebuilds the states for a format; false when the format is unusable.
Every stage off leaves the processor inactive and Process a no-op.

members.name: Reset
members.doc:
Forgets what the canceller and the noise estimate have learned — after a
device change the room and the microphone are different.

members.name: GetAutoGainDb

types.name: FVoiceRadioFilter
types.doc:
FVoiceRadioFilter — what makes a voice sound like it came out of a handheld:
the telephone band, 300 Hz to 3.4 kHz. One low-pass cannot do it (the
low end is the half that says "small speaker"), so this is a high-pass and a
low-pass in series, each a second-order Butterworth section, followed by a
soft clip that leaves speech alone and flattens a shout, the overdriven edge
a radio speaker has.

Stateful per stream: a filter shared between two talkers would smear one
voice's history into the other's first samples.

types.name: IVoiceDecoder
types.doc:
One speaker's decoding state. A stateful codec (Opus predicts each frame
from the ones before it) needs a decoder per stream: a single decoder fed
several speakers interleaved predicts every frame from someone else's voice,
which degrades audibly from the third player on and leaves loss recovery
with nothing coherent to recover from. Frames must reach it in sequence
order, which is why the jitter buffer holds packets and decodes at playout.

members.name: Decode
members.signature: virtual bool Decode(const uint8_t* data, size_t len, std::vector<int16_t>& out) = 0
members.doc: Decodes one payload into exactly the codec's frame size.

members.name: DecodeFec
members.signature: virtual bool DecodeFec(const uint8_t* nextPacket, size_t len, std::vector<int16_t>& out)
members.doc: Rebuilds the frame immediately BEFORE `nextPacket` from its inband FEC.

members.name: DecodeRedundancy
members.signature: virtual bool DecodeRedundancy(const uint8_t* packet, size_t len, uint32_t framesBack, std::vector<int16_t>& out)
members.doc:
Rebuilds the frame `framesBack` frames before `packet` from its deep
redundancy (Opus DRED). False when the packet carries none, or not that
far back.

members.name: Conceal
members.doc:
Synthesises a frame for a hole nothing covers (packet-loss concealment
that continues the decoder's own signal). False when the codec has none
and the caller should fall back to its own concealment.

members.name: CreateDecoder
members.doc: A fresh per-stream decoder. Never shared between speakers.

members.name: GetMaxEncodedBytes
members.doc:
Upper bound on the encoded size of one frame. Callers reserve against
this once so the steady state never reallocates.

members.name: EncodeFrame
members.signature: virtual bool EncodeFrame(const int16_t* samples, uint32_t sampleCount, std::vector<uint8_t>& out) = 0
members.doc:
Encodes exactly GetFrameSamples() samples into `out` (cleared first,
never grown past GetMaxEncodedBytes). False on a wrong sample count.

members.name: DecodeFrame
members.signature: virtual bool DecodeFrame(const uint8_t* data, size_t len, std::vector<int16_t>& out) = 0
members.doc:
Decodes one payload back into exactly GetFrameSamples() samples.
False on a truncated or malformed payload — a hostile peer must not be
able to talk the decoder into writing an unbounded block.

members.name: SupportsInbandFec
members.doc:
True when the codec embeds a coarse copy of the previous frame in every
payload, so one lost frame can be rebuilt from its successor instead of
concealed.

members.name: DecodeFecFrame
members.signature: virtual bool DecodeFecFrame(const uint8_t*, size_t, std::vector<int16_t>&)
members.doc:
Reconstructs the frame that PRECEDES `nextPacket` out of the redundancy
inside it, and must run before `nextPacket` itself is decoded — the
decoder walks the two in order. False when the codec carries no
redundancy, or this packet happens to carry none.
